Ready-made validation rules

Source: R/rule_lib.R
rmbl_rule_library.Rd

Constructors for the checks most schemas need, each returning a rule() that validate_rules() evaluates. Use rule() directly for anything not covered here. Writing the common checks once, here, avoids the off-by-one or the forgotten NA that makes a hand-written rule pass silently, and gives every failure a readable message and the rows that failed.

Usage

rule_in_set(column, set, na_pass = TRUE, severity = c("warning", "fatal"))

rule_between(column, lo, hi, na_pass = TRUE, severity = c("warning", "fatal"))

rule_not_null(column, severity = c("warning", "fatal"))

rule_unique(column, severity = c("warning", "fatal"))

rule_regex(column, pattern, na_pass = TRUE, severity = c("warning", "fatal"))

rule_increasing(column, strictly = FALSE, severity = c("warning", "fatal"))

rule_within_n_mads(
  column,
  n = 3,
  na_pass = TRUE,
  severity = c("warning", "fatal")
)

rule_complete_rows(severity = c("warning", "fatal"))

rule_distinct_rows(columns = NULL, severity = c("warning", "fatal"))

rule_col_count(n, severity = c("warning", "fatal"))

Arguments

column

Character scalar, the name of the column the rule applies to.

set

Vector of allowed values (rule_in_set()); compared as text.

na_pass

Logical scalar, default TRUE: treat NA as passing (see above); FALSE makes a missing value fail.

severity

"warning" (the default) or "fatal": how validate_rules() and the capsule gate treat a failure.

lo, hi

Numeric scalars, the inclusive bounds (rule_between()); lo must not exceed hi.

pattern

Character scalar, the regular expression the values must match (rule_regex()); only the first element is used.

strictly

Logical scalar, default FALSE: require a strict increase rather than non-decreasing (rule_increasing()).

n

Numeric scalar: the multiplier for rule_within_n_mads() (default 3), or the expected number of columns for rule_col_count() (a whole number, no default).

columns

Character vector of columns that jointly must be unique (rule_distinct_rows()), or NULL (the default) for all of them.

Value

A rule() object: a list of class c("bricklayer_rule", "list") with name, expr (the predicate function), column (NULL for whole-table rules), severity and message.

Details

What each rule checks:

  • rule_in_set(): each value, compared as text, is one of set (so 1 and "1" match). Name "<column>_in_set".

  • rule_between(): each value lies in [lo, hi], ends included. Name "<column>_between".

  • rule_not_null(): no value is NA. Name "<column>_not_null".

  • rule_unique(): no value repeats an earlier one; the rows reported are the repeats, not the first occurrence. Two NAs count as a repeat. Name "<column>_unique".

  • rule_regex(): each value, as text, matches pattern (an extended regular expression, grepl()). Name "<column>_regex".

  • rule_increasing(): the column never decreases from one row to the next (or always increases, with strictly = TRUE); missing steps are skipped. A whole-column check: a failure names no rows. Name "<column>_increasing".

  • rule_within_n_mads(): each value lies within n median absolute deviations (scaled by 1.4826, so comparable to standard deviations for normal data) of the column's median. When the MAD is zero (more than half the values equal) any value other than the median fails. The column must be numeric when the rule is evaluated. Name "<column>_within_mads".

  • rule_complete_rows(): no row has a missing value. Name "complete_rows".

  • rule_distinct_rows(): no row repeats an earlier one on columns (columns not in the data are ignored; when none is present the rule passes). Name "distinct_rows".

  • rule_col_count(): the data have exactly n columns. Name "col_count".

The name is the key of the rule's entry in the list validate_rules() returns, which holds only the rules that failed (with severity, message, and for row-wise rules n_failed and rows). A rule that cannot be evaluated (a missing column, text in a numeric rule) is reported as failed, with the reason in its message.

Errors, at construction: column not a single non-empty string; severity other than "warning" or "fatal"; rule_between() with lo > hi or a missing bound; rule_within_n_mads() with n not positive; rule_col_count() with n not a non-negative whole number.

NA handling is explicit and per-rule, because the right answer differs. rule_not_null() exists precisely to fail on NA. The value rules ( rule_in_set, rule_between, rule_regex, rule_within_n_mads) treat NA as PASSING by default, so that a column's missingness is reported once by rule_not_null() or max_missing_fraction rather than again by every other rule; set na_pass = FALSE to make them fail on it instead.

See also

rule() for an arbitrary predicate, validate_rules() to evaluate them, infer_schema() for the structural checks that need no rules at all.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  id = c(1, 2, 2),
  grade = c("a", "b", "z"),
  score = c(5, 200, 7),
  email = c("a@b.com", "nope", "c@d.org"),
  day = c(3, 1, 2),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

rules <- list(
  rule_unique("id", severity = "fatal"),
  rule_in_set("grade", c("a", "b", "c")),
  rule_between("score", 0, 100),
  rule_regex("email", "^[^@]+@[^@]+\\\\.[a-z]+$"),
  rule_increasing("day")
)
names(validate_rules(df, rules))
#> [1] "id_unique"      "grade_in_set"   "score_between"  "email_regex"   
#> [5] "day_increasing"

# Each names the rows that failed.
validate_rules(df, rules)$grade_in_set$rows
#> [1] 3

# Clean data passes every one of them.
ok <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3, grade = c("a", "b", "c"),
  score = c(5, 50, 7),
  email = c("a@b.com", "c@d.org", "e@f.net"),
  day = 1:3, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
length(validate_rules(ok, rules))
#> [1] 1

# A robust outlier rule: MADs from the median, not standard
# deviations from the mean, so one wild value cannot hide the others.
validate_rules(
  data.frame(v = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 900)),
  rule_within_n_mads("v", 5)
)$v_within_mads$rows
#> [1] 6

# Whole-table rules.
validate_rules(df, rule_distinct_rows())
#> list()
validate_rules(df, rule_col_count(5))
#> list()
validate_rules(df, rule_complete_rows())
#> list()

# NA fails only when asked to
g <- data.frame(grade = c("a", NA, "b"))
length(validate_rules(g, rule_in_set("grade", c("a", "b"))))
#> [1] 0
validate_rules(g, rule_in_set("grade", c("a", "b"), na_pass = FALSE))$grade_in_set$rows
#> [1] 2

# bounds are checked when the rule is made
try(rule_between("score", 100, 0))
#> Error : need `lo` <= `hi`, both non-missing
